ELUCIDATION
OF
REGIONAL REGULATION OF TAMBRAUW REGENCY
NUMBER 3 OF 2016
CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL
The State has the obligation to provide Protection to every citizen in accordance with the preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. That Women and Children are among vulnerable groups who tend to experience violence and therefore need to receive protection. Violence against Women and Children constitutes a violation of human rights and therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed without discrimination.

Violence is any act unlawfully with or without the use of means against physical and psychological aspects that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. Furthermore, Violence against Women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering or hardship to Women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. Violence against Children is any act against Children that results in suffering or hardship physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of Children. The existence of Women and Children Victims of Violence has not yet received adequate services and therefore minimum services for Victims of Violence are required.

In order to prevent and overcome Violence against Women and Children in Badung Regency so as to avoid Violence, threats of Violence, torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence in the form of a Regional Regulation.

This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for Women and Children Victims of Violence specifically in terms of services, monitoring and evaluation, reporting, funding, guidance and supervision of Women and Children Victims of Violence in Badung Regency.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE
Article 1
Sufficiently clear.

CHAPTER VII
INSTITUTIONAL ARRANGEMENTS
Article 13
In the context of providing protection services to women and children victims of violence, the Regional Government establishes P2TP2A as an integrated service center for the protection of women and children from acts of violence including victims of acts of violence.
P2TP2A as referred to in paragraph (1) functions as an integrated service center in providing protection to women and children from acts of violence.
P2TP2A as referred to in paragraph (1) above consists of the Health Office, Hospital, Police, Social Affairs Office, Manpower Office, Women's Empowerment and Family Planning Office, Non-Governmental Organizations.
P2TP2A as referred to in Community Organizations, Social Community Organizations, Universities in paragraph (3) shall be established by Regent's Decree.
P2TP2A of Tambrauw Regency in carrying out its duties and functions may coordinate with a network of service units and competent parties in undertaking efforts to protect women and children from acts of violence.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by: Region is Tambrauw Regency.
Regional Government is the Regional Head as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of governmental affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
Regent is the Regent of Tambrauw.
Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is a regional people's representative institution that is positioned as an element of Regional Government administration.
Discrimination is any differentiation, harassment and exclusion that is direct or indirect based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs that result in the reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and basic freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural fields and other aspects of life.
Violence is any act that results in or causes misery and suffering whether physical, sexual, psychological including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or in private life.
Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether in the domestic realm or public in private life.
Violence against children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.
Domestic violence is any act against a person, especially women, that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and or household neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion or unlawful deprivation of freedom within the household sphere.
Trafficking in Persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud and abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited.
Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age including a child in the womb.
Woman is an adult human of female gender and a person who is recognized by law as a woman.
Prevention is activities carried out to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children.
Protection is all service actions to guarantee and protect the rights of victims of acts of violence organized by the Integrated Service Center.
Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage or fainting and or causes death.
Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, distrust or severe psychological suffering to a person.
Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, whether unnatural or unwanted with another person for commercial purposes and or certain purposes.
Victim is a woman and child who experiences acts of violence.
Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence.
Assistance is activities and actions carried out by assistants during the service process.
Assistant is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to provide assistance.
Institution is an agency/institution/body/within the scope of regional government and/or Non-Governmental Organization (NGO) that provides assistance.
Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is an institution providing services to victims of violence based in hospitals, managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psychosocial and legal services.
Safe House is a temporary residence, provided to give protection to victims in accordance with predetermined standards.
Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is an integrated service forum established by the Regional Government in the context of protection services for victims of violence against women and children in Tambrauw Regency.

REGENT OF TAMBRAUW
WEST PAPUA PROVINCE
REGIONAL REGULATION OF TAMBRAUW REGENCY
NUMBER 3 YEAR 2016
CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE
BY THE GRACE OF ALMIGHTY GOD
REGENT OF TAMBRAUW,

Considering : that acts and treatment of violence against women and children constitute actions that violate the rights and dignity of women and children as human beings;
that the implementation of prevention and protection for women and children as victims of acts of violence in Tambrauw Regency has not been optimally carried out thus far;
that based on the considerations as referred to in letter a and letter b, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation concerning Protection of Women and Children From Acts of Violence;

In View of :

Article 2
Letter a Sufficiently Clear Letter b What is meant by "respect for the rights of victims" is a series of actions to respect, appreciate and ensure the fulfillment of the rights of victims.
Letter c What is meant by "justice and gender equality" is a process to be fair to men and women and equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings, so as to be able to play a role and participate in political, economic, social and cultural activities, National defense and security and equality in enjoying the results of such development.
Letter d Sufficiently Clear Letter e What is meant by "non-discrimination" is an attitude and treatment toward victims by not making distinctions based on age, sex, race, ethnicity, religion and between groups.
Letter f What is meant by "the best interests of victims" is all best actions concerning victims carried out by Regional Government, society, legislative bodies and judicial bodies, so that the best interests of victims must be the primary consideration.

3.4.rationale: In the original Indonesian text, “Rumah Aman” is only defined in Pasal 1 as “tempat tinggal sementara… untuk memberikan perlindungan terhadap korban…”. However, the operative provisions on services (Pasal 12) list complaint, medical, medico-legal, legal aid, empowerment, and social rehabilitation services—without mentioning provision/operation of a shelter/safe house. The institutional provisions (Pasal 13) establish P2TP2A but also do not state that it provides/operates a Rumah Aman. So the judge’s “No” is consistent with the actual regulatory commitments; the golden “Yes” appears to have been inferred from a definition rather than an obligation/service.

3.8.evaluator_rationale: Although services are to be implemented by relevant agencies including the "mental and spiritual" field, the provided sentences do not explicitly describe religious/spiritual counselling, guidance, mentoring, or faith-based psychosocial support as a service for victims.

3.8.rationale: The original Indonesian text does not explicitly provide religious/spiritual counselling as a victim service. Pasal 12 enumerates service types (pengaduan, medis, medikolegal, bantuan hukum, pemberdayaan/kemandirian, rehabilitasi sosial) and then says implementation is by SKPD in several fields including “mental dan spriritual” (typo in text). This indicates which agencies/sectors may implement the listed services, but it does not itself add a distinct service of spiritual/religious counselling (“konseling rohani/keagamaan”, “bimbingan rohani”, etc.). Therefore the judge’s “No” is reasonable on the Indonesian ground truth, and the golden “Yes” likely over-interprets the phrase “mental dan spiritual” as an explicit counselling service.
